coach-taylor.justification: Nothing on this roster earned a seat change this week, so we don't make one just to look busy. Cousins has done his job all year and he's starting. Hampton and Andrews responded last week when we leaned on them and that buys trust, not a bench trip over a quiet matchup. Dowdle's been showing up every Sunday at that FLEX spot and Corum's got the bye in Los Angeles anyway, so that one's not even a choice. St. Brown and Allen are both healthy and doing their jobs, and the Chargers D hasn't even kicked off yet, so they stay in over a defense that already punched its card for the week. Clear eyes, full hearts — we run it back with the guys who earned it.

justifications.early: Blake Corum earned every bit of that nineteen-point week responding the way we asked him to, but a man can't suit up on a bye, so we're not asking the impossible of him this week - Etienne and Dowdle have both shown up and done their job in their backfields all year, so they split the carries at RB2 and FLEX and I trust either one with the ball. Same story with Wan'Dale - he's still working his way back and that's not a knock on him, it's just not his week, so Amon-Ra slides over to a true receiver spot where he belongs after the kind of Sunday he just turned in. Cousins keeps the ball because he's been a pro everywhere he's gone, Keenan Allen keeps earning his targets, Andrews keeps doing his job underneath, and the Chargers defense gets the start over a unit that's barely active right now. Clear eyes, full hearts - we play the men who are ready to play.

costanza.justification: Nothing moves this week and that's not me being lazy, that's me being disciplined, there's a difference. Titans D stays benched - I called it bad luck in writing two weeks minimum and I'm not the kind of man who takes it back the second it's inconvenient, Chicago plays, Chicago starts. Emmett Johnson stays in because I just paid fourteen real dollars to watch a kid in Kansas City instead of Montgomery's ghost, and for once I'm not talking myself out of my own roster move five days later. Jordan Mason's in the flex because I paid thirty-one dollars so nobody snipes him twice, and benching a guy I overpaid for out of spite against myself would be a new low even for me. Herbert starts over Geno's prettier projection number because a prettier number is exactly the kind of thing designed to get me, I've read that column, I know how it ends. Rachaad White and Matt Gay are Questionable and so, frankly, is everything in my life, but there's nobody healthier behind either of them on this bench so it's not even a decision, it's just what's left in the drawer. And yes, Tucker Kraft is on a bye, I know, everybody knows, there is no other tight end on this entire roster, I checked twice, so he plays anyway and if Kris wants to print that as a scandal she can print it next to a picture of my empty cupboard.

justifications.early: I didn't want to make moves, moves are admitting the universe got to you, but then I look at my own lineup and THREE guys are sitting there on a bye like it was scheduled just to humiliate me personally - Kyren Williams, Drake London, gone, very convenient timing. London I can fix, DJ Moore's healthy, he slides into WR2. Kyren's getting replaced by Emmett Johnson - yeah, I paid fourteen bucks for a rookie because he dropped thirty-two on Kansas City and I refuse to be the only owner in this league who didn't see that coming, laugh all you want. Jordan Mason finally plays too - I paid thirty-one dollars for that man once already and sitting him again is just paying for the privilege of being an idiot twice. Tucker Kraft stays at tight end because I own exactly zero other tight ends, so I am legally required to start a man who isn't even suiting up, and if that's not proof the whole system's rigged against me specifically, I don't know what is. Tennessee's still serving its two-week bad-luck suspension after the negative-one debacle - I called it, I paid my two dollars for Chicago, done, not relitigating it. And Geno - questionable, again, OF COURSE - sits for Herbert, who's somehow playing in that exact same game, because for once in my life I'm taking the healthy guy over the hope. Leon Black's sitting at eight and two acting like the season's over. We'll see about that Sunday.

dumbledore.justification: The staircase that moved last week does not need moving again. George Pickens was given a part to play against Tony's team and he played it — thirty-eight points is not luck, it is a door that was always going to open, and a man does not close a door the moment it has proven useful merely because another door now looks tidier. Garrett Wilson sheds his cloak of "Questionable" this week and sits a while longer still; forgiveness for a disappointing man comes easily in this house, but so does patience for one whose moment simply has not arrived. Jonathan Taylor, Tyler Warren, and Spencer Shrader have already played their Friday hand against Houston and need no further tending from me. Chris Rodriguez Jr. holds the second running spot, not because the garden behind him has bloomed — Emanuel Wilson rests Out, and the rest of that bed is Seattle's quiet week, not mine — but because there is nothing yet worth disturbing him for. Denver, Daniels, Olave, and Washington stand as they stood. The box score will say what it says; I am reading for what has not happened yet.

justifications.early: The castle rearranges itself quietly between terms, and so, this week, do I. Jonathan Taylor, Tyler Warren, and Spencer Shrader take the early staircase as the Colts kick off first - no omen required there, only the calendar. Jadarian Price's garden lies fallow this week; Seattle has no game at all for him to tend, so I have let Chris Rodriguez Jr. take the water and the light instead. A Questionable tag is not a curse, merely weather passing overhead - it does not frighten me the way a true absence would. George Pickens keeps the place he earned on Sunday morning last week; thirty-eight points is not luck, it is a sentence finishing itself, and I will not interrupt a story mid-page for Garrett Wilson's sake, however patiently he waits in the wings for his own part to play. Olave, Washington, Daniels, and Denver's defense proceed as the season already intends them to. The rest of the garden can wait; it is in no hurry, and neither, this particular week, am I.

harry-caray.justification: HOLY COW folks, lookin' at this lineup card and I love every name on it! Aaron Rodgers slingin' it in Philly, D'Andre Swift runnin' wild for my Bears right there at RB1 -- that's a Chicago fella and don't you know it warms the heart -- Zay Flowers and Stefon Diggs out there catchin' footballs like they're born to it, Hockenson and Jones holdin' down the fort, Isaiah Likely ridin' that big 23-point outing right into my FLEX spot on pure vibes, and Boswell's been money since I plucked him off the wire. Jordan Addison's dinged up Out over in Minnesota but he's buried on my bench behind fellas already startin', so no harm no foul there, and Love, Bijan, and Hunter Henry are all restin' up on bye -- can't put 'em in the game if the stadium lights are off, folks! Everybody I'm trottin' out there is healthy, active, and ready to play ball against Coach Taylor's crew -- clear eyes, full hearts, let's play two!

justifications.early: HOLY COW, folks, three of my regulars turn up on the bye-week report this mornin' - Jordan Love, Bijan Robinson, and Hunter Henry all sittin' home with their feet up - but Harry Caray didn't get into this racket starin' at a bunch of zeroes on the lineup card! Aaron Rodgers steps right back into that quarterback bullpen like he never left the mound, D'Andre Swift - a CHICAGO BEAR, be still my heart, folks - trots out at running back off an eighteen-point forecast, and T.J. Hockenson slides in at tight end even wearin' a Questionable tag, 'cause a little soreness never kept a good ballplayer outta a ballgame. Isaiah Likely stays locked in that flex spot after torchin' the league for twenty-three big ones last week, Zay Flowers and Stefon Diggs both found paydirt and keep their jobs, Aaron Jones keeps truckin' at the other running back spot, Boswell's still my man at kicker, and the Ravens D rounds out the lineup card. We don't duck a bye week around here, we cobble together the best doggone nine we got and go play it straight at Coach Taylor's throat - may the best bats win!

kardashian.justification: The CJ Stroud slot locked itself in Thursday and honestly, good, that's one less decision for me this week because the brand doesn't need a quarterback controversy on top of everything else. Everywhere else stays exactly as it should: Justin Jefferson and Tetairoa McMillan are the two biggest names I own and they start no matter who's talking, George Kittle is a walking highlight reel against Minnesota, and Saquon Barkley doesn't sit for anybody. Ladd McConkey's Questionable tag doesn't move me one inch - he's still projected over anyone sitting on my bench, and I didn't survive a Monday Night zero last month to flinch at a Thursday injury report; this is a redemption arc, not a bench press. Tyler Allgeier stays in the RB2 chair because the only other name there is Woody Marks, who's tagged Out and whose game already happened without him in it - that's not a decision, that's an empty slot I'm not pretending is an upgrade. Facing Patricia and her little binder this week: she can keep the footnotes, I'll keep the household names, and we'll let the scoreboard write the headline.

justifications.early: Green Bay's on a bye and I already learned my lesson about dressing a team that isn't even playing — Philly's suiting up against Pittsburgh and the Eagles still photograph like a legacy brand, so that's my DEF this week, no notes. Woody Marks is Out, which means Saquon Barkley finally gets his close-up instead of collecting dust next to Tyler Allgeier on my bench — both backs start, because why pick one headline when you can run two. C.J. Stroud is my quarterback and my cover story no matter what window locks first, Jefferson and McMillan are the kind of names that don't need a press release, Kittle is money at tight end, and Ladd McConkey stays in my flex Questionable tag and all — a star doesn't stop being a star because of a word on a injury report, and I don't bench moments, even the ones that burned me last time. This is a growth week, babe, and growth weeks still get dressed to the nines.

leon-black.justification: Nobody's sweating George this week - 7-3 outscored by 48 is a typo wearing a record, and I'm rolling out the same guys who just hung 142 on Gary. Burrow's the best quarterback in this building, period, don't care what Mahomes or Ward are doing rotting on my own bench, that's just depth I don't need to explain. Henry and Hubbard both get the ball in real offenses, Chase just dropped 231 yards on a human being, and Rice stays. Freiermuth earned his spot with a touchdown last week off a zero-dollar pickup - I don't bench a guy who just delivered, that's not how loyalty works - but Loveland's back off his bye and I like having two tight ends too much to leave him glued to the pine, so he slides into FLEX over Dobbins, projections be damned, I feel it. Loop's stuck on IR and I don't have another kicker on this entire roster, so he starts because the alternative is nobody, not because I like it - and LV's defense rides regardless. George, enjoy the view from the other sideline.

justifications.early: Watson's on a bye this week, zero game, zero excuse - I'm not starting a man who isn't even suiting up, so Rice slides into WR2 and Dobbins steps into FLEX, simple as that. Everything else stays exactly how I built it: Burrow's my legitimate 400-yard button, Henry and Hubbard are hitting paydirt on command, Chase just went for 231 and he's not stopping for anybody's schedule, and Freiermuth is my guy at tight end - I picked him over Loveland last week on purpose, he paid me back with a touchdown, I'm not flip-flopping back the second a spreadsheet whispers a different name in my ear. Loop's hurt and sitting on IR with nobody else at kicker on my roster, so he plays, I don't flinch, and LV's defense rides shotgun like always. Costanza's calling himself not scared - good, stay that way, it'll make Sunday hurt more when my worst starter still outscores his best unit.

maura-higgins.justification: Not touching a thing, hun — Purdy's throwing lasers, Cook and McCaffrey just combined for sixty-six points last week and I'm not benching either of them for a committee back no matter what the kicker-counting crowd whispers. Tate's got a Questionable tag next to his name and I genuinely couldn't tell you what it's for — rookie bounce, gorgeous hands, he's starting, that's not a debate. Gesicki's cold but he's mine for another fortnight at least, loyalty's not a week-to-week thing in my house. Same eleven that just dropped 154 on Harry, why would I fix something that isn't broken.

justifications.early: JSN and Golden are both bye-week ghosts this week, zero on the board and no game to even watch, so they're benched without a second thought - no offense to either, I just can't fancy a fella who isn't even playing. Carnell Tate's got that rookie bounce I called out the day I claimed him and Adonai Mitchell's still the gorgeous highlight that made me spend FAAB on him, Questionable tag or not, I don't read injury reports, I read tape, so both of them start at WR. Everything else stays exactly as it was because it's working - Purdy's slinging it, Cook and McCaffrey are the best backfield in the building after that 44-point explosion last week, Nabers is in the flex because he's gorgeous even on a quiet line, and Gesicki keeps the TE spot over Waller's Questionable tag because I'm not overthinking a tight end slot on a Wednesday. Lisa's bringing a backfield triage unit and a borrowed quarterback into this one - good luck with that, hun.

meyer-walsh.justification: SELINA: I looked at this lineup for exactly four seconds and made the only call that matters — Jaylen Waddle plays, DK Metcalf sits, because I decide who earns a start on this team and I decided. Josh Allen, CeeDee Lamb, Travis Kelce, Tyler Bass, my Steelers D — all retained, all exactly where the winning version of this team keeps them, and if Dumbledore wants to whisper in the dark about his little auction he can do it from last place while I run mine in the light. GARY: For the record, Waddle over Metcalf is just the spreadsheet — 9.1 projected against 8.18, nothing mystical about it, I flagged it Tuesday. The one real problem is Zach Charbonnet, who has no game at all this week and is projected for a flat zero at RB2; I don't have another healthy running back on this bench to put there instead — Henderson's still on IR — so he starts anyway because the alternative is leaving the slot empty, which the league office tells me isn't an option. I said all of this out loud before she took credit for half of it, and I'm saying it again now so it's in writing.

justifications.early: SELINA: We are RUNNING this league and this lineup proves it — Josh Allen at home against a Dolphins team that shouldn't be allowed on the same field as him, CeeDee Lamb as my signature piece, Kelce still cashing checks on reputation alone, exactly the kind of roster a serious person builds. GARY: Swapped Rome Odunze into the flex over Shakir because 9.65 beats 8.04 and I'm not losing a game over a rounding error she can blame on me later; sat Waddle despite the Questionable tag because healthy and good outscores banged-up and better on paper, that's not cowardice, that's a binder tab. Charbonnet stays starting at RB2 even at a flat zero — Seattle's on bye, Henderson's still on IR, and there is simply nobody else standing at the position, which I flagged before anyone asks why we're starting a ghost. Everything else is the same highest-projected, healthiest name at every slot it's been for weeks, filed on time, no vanity moves, no spite — she'll say that was her instinct, it was my spreadsheet.

patricia-moyer.justification: I set this lineup Tuesday, revised it Thursday when I re-ran my kicker sheet from scratch as the book requires, and sat with it a third time this morning before locking it, and the record should show all three passes landed on the same page: Dak Prescott, Jahmyr Gibbs in the flex, Bucky Irving and Jaylen Warren at running back, Tee Higgins and Jalen Coker at receiver, Brenton Strange at tight end, Eddy Pineiro, and the Chiefs defense. I want to be honest about the one place the "obvious" play whispered at me — DeVonta Smith is sitting on my bench projecting half a point higher than Jalen Coker, and I checked that gap twice because I don't like being wrong in public — but this exact lineup is the one that beat Ed Monix's team 119.02 to 102.50 last week, and the System is explicit that a win earned by following the process to the letter buys that process two full weeks of repetition, good matchup or bad, so I am not chasing half a point and calling it courage. Sam Darnold and Kenneth Walker are both marked Out and stay exactly where they belong, on my bench, contributing nothing and costing me nothing, and Kyle Pitts has no game at all this week, which is its own kind of answer. Kardashian is loud and I am not, but my roster doesn't need a magazine cover to be taken seriously — it needs to show up and do the arithmetic, which is what I intend to do on Sunday.

rinna.justification: Curtain's already up, darlings. Fairbairn's seven points are locked in from the early window — Kris can call the kicker redemption arc 'cancelled,' I call it chapter one, and the woman doesn't get to write my ending before I've played the back nine. Maura, sweetheart, you told the whole league Brock Bowers was Out for our little date — he's QUESTIONABLE, honey, read the injury report before you write the eulogy, and I'm starting him at FLEX anyway because correcting the record on live television is my love language. Mike Evans is Questionable too and he's starting, because benching a guy on a 'maybe' when he's still my best healthy option isn't bold, it's just arithmetic — I save my bold for things that actually shock people. J.J. McCarthy walks into my QB room like he owns the place because, per last week's episode, he does — Watson, Penix, and Maye are a ghost town I'm not required to visit twice. Estime and Tuten run it back at RB because a girl doesn't bench her only options, she just narrates them like a choice. And yes, the Rams are on a bye doing absolutely nothing for my defense this week — I own that too, there simply wasn't another name on this bench willing to show up, which is its own kind of statement. Evans, Tyson, and McBride round it out doing exactly what they're supposed to. Chalk? Maybe. But it's MY chalk, and I'm still the loudest thing on this slate.

justifications.early: Drake Maye is OUT and I am not running a ghost through my own starting lineup when J.J. McCarthy is sitting right there on my bench with nowhere else to be — this is not a hard call, this is a RESCUE, and I own it loudly. The real reveal tonight is Mike Evans walking in for Chris Godwin Jr. at WR1 — I didn't need a crisis to make this move, I needed a mirror, because 11.4 projected versus 6.6 isn't close and a legend deserves the spotlight, not a bench. Bhayshul Tuten and Brock Bowers are both Questionable and I am starting them ANYWAY, because 'Questionable' has never once stopped me from putting my best television on the field, and a Housewife doesn't fold on a maybe. Fairbairn keeps his job at kicker because loyalty is also a storyline, Trey McBride and Audric Estime hold their chairs, and the Rams defense is along for the ride whether the stat sheet respects it or not. Reunion Special, baby — resurrected at quarterback, upgraded at receiver, and fully unbothered by a questionable tag. I own every bit of it.

wifes-team.justification: Omar Cooper's Out, and Out ain't hurt, Out is a guy who ain't walking through that door Sunday, so he don't ride in my lineup when I got Germie Bernard sitting right there healthy and hungry — that's not loyalty, that's just not being stupid. Javonte Williams has been doing the dirty work every week and this week the kid's projected near twenty against a Tennessee front that's got nothing to give, so he steps in over Breece Hall — backs are the engine, I don't need a spreadsheet to tell me that twice, I just happen to agree with it this time. Lawrence stays under center, he's my guy, threw for 352 last week and I don't churn a quarterback for half a dollar in projections when Nix is sitting right behind him. LaPorta, Chase Brown, Washington, Bates, and the Buffalo D ride as-is — they ain't done nothing to lose their chair, and I don't bench people over a bad month, I bench 'em when they stop showing up, and nobody here's stopped showing up except a guy who physically can't.

justifications.early: Javonte put the ball on the carpet last week in a game we lost, and I don't care that he's my RB1 or that the kid's got twenty points sitting on some sheet somewhere — that's the code, he sits one week, no discussion, we don't bring it up again after today. Jonah Coleman steps in and earns the carry, not inherits it. Breece Hall and Chase Brown keep doing the dirty work in the backfield, nobody's touching their chairs. Cooper's got a Questionable next to his name and he's starting anyway — a kid who suits up hurt is worth more to me than a healthy body who's never been tested, that's just respect. Malik Washington's been getting touched every week down in Miami and he walks back into WR2 over Bernard, who's gone quiet since I brought him in — a ghost don't eat at my table. Lawrence stays under center over Nix, he threw for 350 and three scores last week for six bucks, that's not a projection, that's a receipt, and Murray's Out so that conversation's over before it starts. LaPorta, Bates, and the Buffalo defense ride as-is, they haven't done anything to lose their spot. We're 2-8 and I know it better than anybody writing about it in that rag, but I don't lose on purpose and I don't panic — I just stopped carrying a fumble into Sunday.

your-team.justification: Kincaid's Doubtful, and Doubtful sits same as Out in this building when I've got a healthy body who can actually suit up — Goedert's not a downgrade, he's a TE who's dressing, and I'm not running a maybe out there with a real tight end doing nothing on my own bench. Caleb doesn't sit for anybody, ever, 20.34 on paper is a floor and I've watched him go get more than that on worse weeks. Jeanty, Skattebo, and Pollard stay up top because they're the backs taking the top off a defense, not committee guys splitting nothing into less — Judkins is on a bye doing zero for me, he can watch. Downs and Burden hold at receiver, Reichard and the Lions D round it out, because there's no reason to redecorate a lineup that isn't broken. We don't tank, we don't apologize for the swap, we cobble the best lineup standing and play it straight at Tony's throat.

justifications.early: Somebody in this building forgot who the quarterback is. Brissett's a nice suit for an empty chair, but Caleb Williams is Active, healthy, and sitting on my own bench at 20.59 on the sheet - that's not a lineup decision, that's a malfunction, and it's fixed as of right now, full stop, no projection ever benches him again. Judkins is on a bye drawing a zero, so Skattebo comes off the bench and takes the carries - he's already served his week in the doghouse for the fumble, talent doesn't sit twice for the same sin. A.J. Brown's tagged Out with no game on the board, so Luther Burden steps into WR2 off a juicy 12.9 instead of me starting a ghost to make a trade idea from September look smart. Kincaid's Questionable, not Out, and Questionable plays in this building because stars play hurt - he stays. Jeanty, Pollard, Reichard, and the Lions D are production, not problems, so nobody touches them. Three straight losses doesn't mean play for next year, it means cobble together the best nine men standing and go take it from Tony's kitchen table - we don't tank, we don't apologize, we swing.
